seo_title: Cost of Living in Thessaloniki 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Thessaloniki per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: Greece's second city on the shore of the gulf: a rich history, a student vibe and excellent cuisine. Cheaper than Athens; Russian citizens need a Schengen visa, and in winter it can get cool and windy.
pros: Cheaper than Athens and many European capitals
A rich history and a student, lively atmosphere
Excellent Greek cuisine and coffee houses
The sea within the city and a long warm season
A convenient base for trips around northern Greece
cons: Russian citizens need a Schengen visa
In winter it can get cool and windy
European prices for rent and groceries

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Thessaloniki?
faq.answer: Yes, you need a Schengen visa — Greece is part of the Schengen Area.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Thessaloniki?
faq.answer: Cheaper than Athens and the islands, but prices are European. The exact budget is in the calculator above.

faq.question: Which language is spoken in Thessaloniki?
faq.answer: Greek; thanks to students and tourism, English is widespread.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Thessaloniki?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You'll need a foreign bank card or euros in cash.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Thessaloniki?
faq.answer: Mediterranean with a continental touch: hot summers and winters cooler than in the south.

faq.question: How is Thessaloniki different from Athens?
faq.answer: Thessaloniki is more compact, cheaper and younger in spirit, with the sea right in the city centre.

reviews.text: Thessaloniki is an underrated city: history, the sea and student energy, cheaper than Athens. The downside for Russians — the Schengen and the winter wind off the gulf.
I fell in love with the coffee houses and the waterfront. The city is lively and cosy, prices lower than on the islands. The difficulty — the visa and gathering documents for a long stay.
